guidance.statement: We do see that around 14 to 15% of growth, overall growth, 1 and 2% here and there. We feel that we are very well placed to grow.

status_history.evidence: FY27 credit growth guidance now 13-14%, against 14-16% given in May 2026.

guidance.statement: Credit growth of 13% to 14%, which management calls the minimum.
NIM to be maintained around 3.3% to 3.4%.
ROA around 1.4% to 1.5% in the next two to three quarters, ~1.46% by year end.
Corporate loan book to grow 12% to 13% by end of year.
GIFT City branch to build a book of around USD 500 million by end of FY27.

industry: Financial Services > Banks > Public Sector Bank

operating_notes.text: Total business stood at ₹6,78,614 crores as of 31st March 2026.
Board approved FY27 capital plan including up to ₹5,000 Cr equity raise and ₹1,000 Cr Basel III Tier II bonds.
Received perpetual license from IFSCA to set up an IFSC Banking Unit at GIFT IFSC, Gujarat.
Total SMA stood at ₹13,000 Cr (4.05% of credit) as of June 2026, down ₹2,200 Cr from March.
ECLGS universe is ~₹4,400 Cr, with ₹2,600 Cr disbursed and ₹1,800 Cr expected by August-September.
CGTMSE-covered loans are around 15-16% of the total credit portfolio.
Received SEBI approval to issue up to 10 crore fresh equity shares to eligible employees via ESPS for MPS compliance.
RBI ISE 2026 observations on risk weights for syndicated ECB loans adjusted Total CRAR to 19.06% as of March 31, 2026.
Investment Fluctuating Reserve (IFR) balance of ₹490 Cr was transferred to Revenue Reserve in Q1FY27 following revised RBI directions.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): interest earned ₹8,488.96 Cr (+11.2% YoY), net profit ₹1,505.45 Cr (+37.9% YoY).
Indian Overseas Bank reported FY26 net profit of ₹5,208 Cr with GNPA improving to 1.42% during the analyst meet on May 8, 2026.
Indian Overseas Bank's board approved a capital plan for FY27 featuring up to ₹5,000 Cr in equity raising and ₹1,000 Cr in Basel III Tier II bonds.
Indian Overseas Bank received the perpetual license from IFSCA on June 1, 2026, to establish an IFSC Banking Unit at GIFT City, Gujarat.
Indian Overseas Bank received SEBI approval to issue up to 10 crore fresh equity shares to employees via an ESPS to comply with minimum public shareholding norms.
Indian Overseas Bank disclosed RBI Inspection for Supervisory Evaluation (ISE) 2026 risk weight adjustments resulting in a Total CRAR of 19.06% as of March 31, 2026.
Indian Overseas Bank board approved the Q2 and H1 FY27 financial results on October 26, 2026.

status_history.evidence: GNPA at 1.33% as on June 2026, below the 1.42% FY26 level.

watchlist.response: SMA percentage to total credit came down from 6.70% in March 2025 to 4.92% in March 2026. No stress seen so far from West Asia crisis.

status_history.evidence: SMA disclosed at ₹13,000 Cr (4.05%), down ₹2,200 Cr QoQ; no West Asia stress seen.

watchlist.text: SMA numbers were not disclosed in the presentation and potential stress from West Asian crisis on MSME/export clients.
Statutory approvals for the ₹5,000 Cr equity raise

watchlist.response: Management did not explain the adjustment, answering instead on credit growth and ROA guidance.
watchlist.text: Book value per share disclosed at ₹15.79 versus ~₹20.5 computed from net worth divided by shares.

watchlist.response: Attributed to exiting one ~₹10,000 Cr account on pricing in April; expects 12-13% corporate growth by year end.
Said mostly regularised, pointing to the 0.06% slippage ratio.
